summary: Iteration 4 — frontend QA of the re-directed ArchiveScene (scroll-scrubbed title sequence) + requested regression sweep. Method: hard reload per viewport, window.__lenis.scrollTo(y,{immediate:true}) + 1.9s settle, pin base read dynamically from the GSAP pin-spacer (1920x800 base=20960 as expected, span=11.5*innerHeight), clip-path/circle-aware effective-opacity probe on all 20 .ax-* layers. Depth sweep at 1920x800 across 30 depths, 1920x1080/1440x900/1366x768 spot checks, mobile 430x932 / 390x844 / 375x812, plus a full reverse scrub 0.95->0.02. Beats A,B,C,D,E(travel),F,G,H,I,J(silence/foot lines/exit wipe) all render at the expected depths, element budget holds (never 2+ photographs visible at any depth: hero alone, aperture alone, or slit alone), z-order is correct (aperture z45 above black z40, slit z10 covers ARCHIVE z5, IS JUST z30 in front), zero horizontal overflow at every viewport, nothing stuck at d=0.02 (only meta + tiny hero + crops) or after the pin (transit scene works, archive fully cleared). 3 real defects found: (1) beat E's resolve is invisible behind the F splice, (2) BEGINNING. does not come back on reverse scrub in beat I, (3) the final resolved statement reads THE ARCHIVE / BEGINNING. / IS JUST (wrong order + glyph overlap + bottom clipping) at 1920-wide viewports. Regression all green: pytest 9/9, nav anchors, ripple START -> /start with 0 leftover overlays, /start USD<->INR toggle ($3,000-$6,000 -> Rs2.5L-Rs5L), console error-free (only the benign 'scale not eligible for reset' warning).

ui_bugs.issue: At 1920-wide viewports the statement resolves out of order and overlapping: measured 1920x800 -> THE ARCHIVE t224-397, BEGINNING. t446-706, IS JUST t664-821 (IS JUST sits BELOW BEGINNING, glyph boxes overlap ~42px and IS JUST is clipped by the 800px viewport bottom); 1920x1080 -> arch3 302-475, beg 648-907, just 810-966 (~97px overlap). Correct order at 1440x900, 1366x768 and all mobile widths, so the vh-based y offsets (.ax-beg y:22vh vs .ax-just y:2vh) do not hold for the vw-scaled type at >=1600px width. Screenshot-confirmed.

The 'resolve to small readable ARCHIVE + THE' moment is never visible: the resolve tween runs 10.0-10.9 (d 0.440-0.480) while .ax-black reaches opacity 1 at t=10.52 (d=0.463). Measured at d=0.470/0.475: giant is the small resolved word (552x142 / 429x111 at ~600-740px) and .ax-the-s is at op 0.9, but both are fully covered by black op=1. At d=0.452 the word is still mid-travel (3995px wide, off-canvas left). Beat E therefore cuts to black before the payoff frame exists.

BEGINNING. is not restored on reverse scrub. Forward at d=0.70: .ax-beg op=0.693 (t495-913, cropped below viewport). After scrubbing to d=0.95 and back to d=0.70: .ax-beg is fully invisible (reproduced twice). Cause: two competing fromTo tweens on .ax-beg autoAlpha (15.1 fade-in 0->0.9 and 20.0 fromTo 0->1 with from y:92vh/scale:1.45); the later fromTo's 'from' values win on reverse. Violates the 'all scrubbed and reversible' rule.

BEGINNING. is still entirely below the viewport at d=0.90 (measured t=907-1317, off-screen) so the frame is empty; the cropped rise only becomes visible from d~0.915. Brief expects the rising cropped BEGINNING at d~0.90.

Brief asks for ARCHIVE to exceed screen width with controlled clipping on mobile; measured .ax-arch2 width 372px @390, 410px @430, i.e. it stays inside the viewport (text-[24vw]) and is never clipped.

issues: IS JUST (orange) collides with the BEGINNING. outline and is cut off by the viewport bottom edge — the composition reads incorrectly

action_items: Fix beat J resolve layout for wide viewports: drive .ax-just / .ax-beg / .ax-arch3 vertical positions off a shared, aspect-aware scale (or use px/clamp offsets) so the order is always THE ARCHIVE / IS JUST / BEGINNING. with no overlap and nothing clipped at 1920x800 and 1920x1080.
Give beat E's resolved small ARCHIVE + THE a visible hold (e.g. move .ax-black on to ~10.9-11.0 or finish the resolve by ~10.4) so the payoff frame is seen before the hard cut.
Make .ax-beg reversible: split the beat-I and beat-J appearances into separate elements, or replace the second fromTo with set()+to() so a reverse scrub restores the beat-I opacity.
critical_code_review_comments: Two fromTo tweens targeting the same autoAlpha on .ax-beg is the root cause of the reverse-scrub loss; prefer explicit .set() at the beat start + .to() for reversible scrubbed timelines.

Mixing vw-based font sizes with vh-based y offsets makes beat I/J compositions aspect-ratio dependent — the 1920x800 and 1920x1080 breakages come from this; consider clamp()/px offsets derived from the measured type height.
ArchiveScene.jsx is 370 lines and readable, but the desktop and mobile timelines duplicate ~40 lines of beat structure; extracting the shared beat helpers would reduce drift between the two.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Pin base at 1920x800 = 20960 (read it dynamically from the pin-spacer, it changes per viewport: 1440x900=23580, 1366x768=20122, 1920x1080=28296, 390x844=22114, 430x932=24418, 375x812=21274). span = 11.5*innerHeight desktop, 6.8*innerHeight mobile; t = d*22.7 / d*13.25. Retest priorities after fixes: d=0.95 order/clipping at 1920x800 AND 1920x1080, d 0.46-0.48 for the beat-E payoff, and the reverse 0.95->0.70 .ax-beg opacity.
rca_of_the_issue: 1) Beat J order: .ax-just (md:text-[34vw], 653px line box at 1920) is scaled 0.24 with y:2vh while .ax-beg (md:text-[15vw]) uses y:22vh — because the type height scales with vw and the offsets with vh, at >=1600px width the scaled IS JUST centre lands ~250px lower than BEGINNING, inverting the reading order and pushing IS JUST past the 800px viewport bottom. 2) Beat E: .ax-black autoAlpha 1 completes at t=10.52 while the .ax-giant resolve tween runs to t=10.9 and .ax-the-s only reaches op 0.9 at 10.55, so the resolved frame only ever exists behind the opaque splice. 3) .ax-beg has two fromTo tweens on autoAlpha; on reverse the later fromTo (t=20.0, from autoAlpha 0) re-applies its from-state and the earlier beat-I fade-in is not re-rendered, leaving the element invisible at d=0.70 on the way back.
